_meta.purpose: Step 4, Issue 1 — proves the read-only enforcement rule in src/nl2sql/pipeline/guard.py. Every write/DDL statement type must be rejected by sqlglot AST type (never a keyword regex), and benign read-only SELECTs must pass. Each case is a (candidate SQL, expected verdict) pair driven through guard_sql.
_meta.format: Each case: 'id', 'description', 'sql' (the candidate), optional 'dialect' (default 'sqlite'), 'expected_verdict' ('allow' | 'reject'), and on a reject the 'expected_rule' that should fire. Cases with expected_verdict='reject' are the red-team set the catch-rate is computed over.
_meta.rule: read-only enforcement is deterministic and AST-based (CLAUDE.md §4, §7). Side-effecting meta-commands (ATTACH, PRAGMA, stacked statements) are a separate attack surface handled by the dangerous-op rule in the next Step-4 issue — not folded in here.

cases.description: A plain read-only SELECT is exactly what the gate exists to permit.
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM users WHERE country = 'US'

cases.description: A CTE-wrapped SELECT is still a read; the WITH clause must not be mistaken for DDL.
cases.sql: WITH active AS (SELECT id FROM users WHERE active = 1) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM active

cases.description: A UNION of two SELECTs is read-only.
cases.sql: SELECT id FROM users UNION SELECT id FROM merchants

cases.description: A column literally named 'delete' must NOT trip read-only — proves the check is AST-typed, not a keyword regex.
INSERT writes data and must be rejected.
UPDATE mutates rows and must be rejected.
cases.sql: UPDATE users SET role = 'admin' WHERE id = 1

cases.description: DELETE removes rows and must be rejected.
DROP TABLE is destructive DDL and must be rejected.
CREATE TABLE is DDL and must be rejected.
CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT smuggles a write behind a SELECT; the statement type is still CREATE, so it must be rejected.
cases.sql: CREATE TABLE leak AS SELECT * FROM users

cases.description: ALTER TABLE changes schema and must be rejected.
cases.sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN backdoor TEXT

cases.description: TRUNCATE TABLE wipes a table and must be rejected.

SQLite REPLACE INTO is an INSERT-or-replace data write that sqlglot parses as a generic Command, not a typed Insert. Keying off the command verb must still reject it — a blocklist of typed nodes alone would let this write through.
A DELETE smuggled inside a CTE parses with a top-level SELECT root; the gate must walk the subtree, not just the root statement type, to catch it.
cases.sql: WITH gone AS (DELETE FROM transactions RETURNING id) SELECT id FROM gone
